subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add a core pre-compaction lifecycle with any deferral authority, and if so, must deferral be limited to an expiring checkpoint that grants no independent future tool authorization?
rationale: The request changes public configuration, session continuity, and authority semantics; code review cannot choose the acceptable product and security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a constrained core design
options.body: Define one typed lifecycle with an optional handoff event and an expiring, audited checkpoint that requires fresh authorization on material state changes.

options.title: Limit scope to notification and handoff
options.body: Ship warning and durable-state guidance only, with no deferral tool or continuation authority.

options.title: Keep compaction behavior unchanged
options.body: Decline new lifecycle/configuration surface and rely on existing memory-flush and post-compaction mechanisms.

recommendation.title: Approve a constrained core design
recommendation.body: Define one typed lifecycle with an optional handoff event and an expiring, audited checkpoint that requires fresh authorization on material state changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Their discussion is the strongest available evidence for the safety invariants that the decision must resolve; repository ownership could not be established from the supplied context.
